messages.subject: Inla prediction to grid using stack only predicts to the first 230 new locations out of > 9 million new locations
parts:
Hi,
I am seeking some help. I've been trying to predict to lose grid consisting of over 9 million locations. I first used inla with SPDE to model the relationship between biomass at 316 locations and soil types (30 types) as a categorical variable. Because not all soil types are present, I have to remove the ones that are not present from the prediction grid (this is why I refer to it as a lose grid). I form a stack to predict to the new locations, but after running for sometime the process ends. Usually with verbose = true, it stops at some point and then I get the message below:

                Predictor                         9969275       2446

  The inla-program exited with an error. Unless you interupted it yourself, please rerun with verbose=TRUE and check the output carefully.

  If this does not help, please contact the developers at <he...@r-inla.org>.

In addition: Warning message:

running command '"C:/Users/Kurt/Documents/R/win-library/3.4/INLA/bin/windows/64bit/inla.exe"  -b -s -v  -t 1  "C:/Users/Kurt/AppData/Local/Temp/Rtmp6rl3GO/fileecc359e775b/Model.ini"' had status 253 "


It has only made it past listing all of the soil levels once. I thought it was a memory issue and have since increased my memory to 64 GB on a machine with two processors and 8 cores. I have used various commands that I've seen in this group to allow for efficient memory use such as: num.threads=1 and control.inla = list(strategy = "gaussian", int.strategy = "eb"). Usually only the first 230 locations have predictions if the process terminates or if i terminate the process after the soil levels are listed above. I would like to know what I'm possibly doing wrong. Below is a sample of my code.


Thanks in advance..



#############

library(INLA)


pts.bound <- inla.nonconvex.hull(est.coord.1, 1.9)

mesh <- inla.mesh.2d(est.coord.1, boundary=pts.bound,cutoff=0.1, offset = c(1, 8.5), max.edge = c(1, 1.5))




#-- Construct the SPDE object --#

spde = inla.spde2.matern(mesh=mesh, alpha = 2)



field.indices = inla.spde.make.index("field", n.spde=mesh$n)


A.est = inla.spde.make.A(mesh, loc=est.coord.1)



######For single variable soil..the best model
stack.est = inla.stack(data = list(AGB=est.data),
A = list(A.est, 1),
effects = list(c(field.indices), data.frame (Intercept=1, soil=biomass4$DOMSOI_12, 
Method = inla.group(biomass4$Method))),
tag="est")

####Method is the method used to estimate biomass..not all entries have a method type assigned.

###removing the default intercept by specifying -1 and replacing it with one called "Intercept"..page 210
formula <- AGB ~ -1 + Intercept + soil + f(Method, model = "iid")+ f(field, model=spde)



#-- Call INLA and get results --#
mod =   inla(formula,
             data=inla.stack.data(stack.est, spde=spde),
             family="gaussian",
             control.predictor=list(A=inla.stack.A(stack.est), compute=TRUE),
 control.fixed=list(expand.factor.strategy="inla"),
             control.compute=list(cpo=TRUE, dic=TRUE),
             keep=FALSE, verbose=TRUE)

mod$dic$dic
print(summary(mod))



####Prediction


Apred6 <- inla.spde.make.A(mesh = mesh, loc = cbind(iDat$X, iDat$Y))



stack.pred.response <-inla.stack(data=list(AGB=NA), A=list(Apred6,1), effects=list(c(field.indices),data.frame(Intercept=1,soil=iDat$DOMSOI_12)), tag = "pred")



join.stack <-inla.stack(stack.est,stack.pred.response)



#-- Call INLA and get results --#

mod =   inla(formula,

             data=inla.stack.data(join.stack, spde=spde),

             family="gaussian",

             control.predictor=list(A=inla.stack.A(join.stack), compute=TRUE),control.inla = list(strategy = "gaussian", int.strategy = "eb"), quantiles=NULL, verbose=TRUE, num.threads=1)

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Inla prediction to grid using stack only predicts to the first 230 new locations out of > 9 million new locations
parts:
With millions of prediction points you are better off doing the predictions outside the inla call, via posterior simulations, as the memory requirement inside inla will be too big.
Inla.posterior.sample() is the function that does the work for that.

To make this process easier, you might consider our new package inlabru, http://inlabru.org/
If you send me your code I might give you some more precise guidance for that.

Finn

On Thursday, July 27, 2017 at 11:08:11 PM UTC-5, Finn Lindgren wrote:

With millions of prediction points you are better off doing the predictions outside the inla call, via posterior simulations, as the memory requirement inside inla will be too big.
Inla.posterior.sample() is the function that does the work for that.

To make this process easier, you might consider our new package inlabru, http://inlabru.org/
If you send me your code I might give you some more precise guidance for that.

Finn
